# brickie

> brickie measures a Rust workspace (module dependency edges, per-function complexity) and checks
> it against rules the maintainers wrote in `brickie.toml`; the rules are the project's
> architecture. This static guide is for coding agents in a repository that uses brickie.

## Workflow

1. `brickie measure` reads the code (cargo metadata, rust-analyzer, tree-sitter) and writes
   `.brickie/cache.json` next to `brickie.toml`. It is slow: run it once per round of edits.
2. `brickie check` reads the cache and rules, prints diagnostics, and exits non-zero on an
   unaccepted error. It is fast and never runs rust-analyzer.
3. Fix the code each diagnostic points at.
4. Re-run `measure`, then `check`, until the exit code is 0.

- After any code change, re-measure before trusting `check`. A `stale/*` warning means the code
  changed since the last measure. Config edits never need a re-measure.
- `brickie check --format json` prints `{summary, diagnostics}`; each finding has `id`, `code`,
  `level`, `brick_level`, `message`, `span`, `spans`, `rule`, `help`, `notes`. Read the text form,
  loop over the JSON.
- `brickie interface <brick-path> [--json]` (for example `root/web/api`) prints the brick's
  declared interface: every item outside code can name, with signature, first doc paragraph,
  definition, and uses (grouped by using brick, file:line:col per site; `[test]` marks test code);
  unused items are marked `UNUSED`. Read it before using or changing a brick from outside.
  `--from <brick-path>` instead lists every reference site from that brick into this one, by used
  item. JSON lists every site; text shows five per using brick.
- `brickie serve` is a web viewer for humans; you do not need it.
- Every command accepts `--config path/to/brickie.toml` (default `./brickie.toml`).

Exit codes of `brickie check`: 0 clean (only warnings or accepted findings), 1 at least one
unaccepted `error`, 2 configuration, review file or cache problem (for example no cache: run
`brickie measure`).

## Hard constraints

- Never edit `brickie.toml` (or files it includes) or `brickie.review.toml` to make `check` pass;
  they are the project's decisions. While a change is open (`brickie change` does not say
  `change/none`), never edit them at all: propose ops (see "Change sessions").
- Accepting a finding (`[[accept]]` in `brickie.review.toml`, or Accept in the viewer) and
  accepting or rejecting a change op are for a human reviewer. If a finding looks wrong or a rule
  too strict, stop and report it with the finding id.
- Do not split a function mechanically to get under a complexity limit (forwarding helpers, one
  statement per function). Reduce real complexity: early returns, a table instead of a branch
  chain, a struct instead of many parameters, a clearer decomposition.
- Do not move code or add re-exports to hide a dependency from the checker; the edge is measured
  where the code references the other module.

## Change sessions

A human designs in the viewer's editor; you work on the same design through a **change**: an
ordered log of operations (ops) over the `brickie.toml` tree, kept in `.brickie/change/`. One
change is open at a time. Config files are not written while it is open, only when the human
publishes.

- Run `brickie change` at the start and before each step. It prints the intent, the status
  (accepted / proposed / rejected / conflicts, cache age), the semantic diff against the config as
  opened (by element, with author, notes and review notes; the human's notes are your
  instructions), and entries new since your last read (it then moves your cursor). `--since <seq>`
  shows entries after `seq` without moving the cursor; `--as human|agent` picks the reader
  (default `agent`).
- `brickie change --todo` lists tasks:
  - `planned`: bricks to create code for (with their members).
  - `drift`: findings the change introduces (`check` over the design minus the findings of the
    design as opened; id, location, help).
  - `link` (`change/planned-edge`): an allow rule the change adds that no measured edge uses yet.
  - `reason` (`change/no-reason`): a rule the change adds without a `reason`.
  - ops `proposed`, `rejected` (with the reason) or in `conflict`.
  - `config`: errors of the design. A cache measured in another workspace gives one `config` task
    (`cache does not match this workspace; run brickie measure`) instead of every brick planned.
- Propose an op: `echo '<op JSON>' | brickie change propose --json [--note "why"]`. It stays
  `proposed` until the human accepts or rejects it; each review is a new entry with its own `seq`
  and note. Never accept or reject ops yourself.
- After code changes run `brickie measure`, then `brickie check --change`: it checks the design
  (accepted and proposed ops) against the code and lists `change/planned` notes.
- When an op of yours is rejected or in conflict, stop and ask the human; do not re-propose it.
  The human may take back their own ops (`brickie change retract [seq]`; the op counts as
  rejected), restore the latest retracted one (`brickie change redo`; refused when it no longer
  applies; a new human op clears what can be redone), or re-record a conflicting op against the
  current design (`brickie change reapply <seq>`: a new human op, the original rejected with note
  `re-applied as op N`).
- `brickie change publish --dry-run` shows what publishing would write and why it would refuse.
  Publishing and `brickie change discard` are the human's decision.
- `--format json` on every `brickie change` command: `brickie change` prints
  `{status, diff, new: {from, head, entries}}`, `--todo` a list of `{kind, text, seq?, id?, help?}`,
  `propose` the op record, `publish --dry-run`
  `{files: [{path, action, note, content?}], blockers, warnings}` (warnings do not block).

An op record is `{seq, by: human|agent, at, op, file, key, before, after, note, state:
proposed|accepted|rejected, review: {seq, by, note}, conflict}`; `file` is the config file it edits
(relative to the root config's directory), `key` the element (`brick:<name>`, `rule:<i>`,
`complexity:<i>`, `exports`, `deps`, `include`, `file`), `before` / `after` its canonical TOML. A
review entry is `{entry: "review", seq, by, at, target, verdict: accept|reject|retract|restore,
note}`.

Ops (`file` is required on each; fields mirror the `brickie.toml` reference below):

```json
{"op": "add_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "brick": {"name": "store", "members": ["path:crates/store/"], "tags": ["core"], "desc": "..."}}
{"op": "remove_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "name": "store"}
{"op": "set_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "name": "store", "desc": "...", "tags": [], "members": [], "path": ""}
{"op": "add_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "brick": {"name": "ui", "kind": "group"}}
{"op": "rename_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "from": "store", "to": "db"}
{"op": "move_brick", "file": "brickie.toml", "name": "db", "into_file": "brickie.toml", "into": "core"}
{"op": "make_composite", "file": "brickie.toml", "name": "db", "path": "crates/db"}
{"op": "ungroup", "file": "brickie.toml", "name": "db"}
{"op": "set_exports", "file": "crates/db/brickie.toml", "exports": [{"brick": "api"}, {"brick": "x", "scope": "test"}]}
{"op": "add_rule", "file": "brickie.toml", "rule": {"from": "app", "to": "db", "action": "allow", "reason": "..."}}
{"op": "set_rule", "file": "brickie.toml", "index": 0, "rule": {"from": "app", "to": "db", "action": "deny"}}
{"op": "remove_rule", "file": "brickie.toml", "index": 0}
{"op": "add_complexity", "file": "brickie.toml", "rule": {"bricks": "tag:core", "cognitive": 15}}
{"op": "set_complexity", "file": "brickie.toml", "index": 0, "rule": {"cognitive": 12}}
{"op": "remove_complexity", "file": "brickie.toml", "index": 0}
{"op": "set_deps", "file": "brickie.toml", "default": "deny", "cycles": "deny"}
{"op": "create_file", "file": "presets/layers.toml"}
{"op": "add_include", "file": "brickie.toml", "path": "presets/layers.toml"}
{"op": "remove_include", "file": "brickie.toml", "path": "presets/layers.toml"}
```

- `kind` (`crate`, `module`, `group`) is optional and kept in the op only. `crate` with no members
  defaults them to `path:crates/<name>/` (`path:<name>/` in a nested file); `group` defaults `path`
  to the name and creates its `brickie.toml`; a `module` needs members (`<crate>::<module>`).
- `move_brick` moves a brick into the children of brick `into` of `into_file` (made a composite
  when it is a leaf) or, without `into`, into the level file `into_file`. `path:` members are
  rebased; moving into a sibling makes the source file's rules on the brick name the sibling.
  Publishing moves no code: the plan lists a moved brick as a manual step.
- `set_brick` changes only the fields given (an empty `desc` or `path` removes it).
- `rename_brick` also renames the brick in the rules, complexity selectors and `exports` of the
  same file.
- `make_composite` sets `path` and creates `<path>/brickie.toml`.
- `ungroup` undoes a composite: its children (`path:` members rebased), `[[deps.rule]]` and
  `[[complexity]]` move into `file`, its `exports` are dropped, and the brick stays a leaf without
  `path`. It refuses when the child file has `include` or `[deps] default`/`cycles`. The child file
  leaves the design; publish never deletes it and lists it as a manual step.
- Rule and complexity `index` count the `[[deps.rule]]` / `[[complexity]]` tables of that one file,
  from 0.

Publishing writes the config files (comments and order kept) and scaffolds the code of added
bricks: the folder of a composite, a crate (`Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, a workspace member) for a
`path:` or unknown package member, or a module (`<module>/mod.rs` and a `pub mod` line in its
parent) for a module member. Existing files are never overwritten. A scaffolded brick stays
planned until the next `brickie measure`.

## Reading a diagnostic

```
error[deps/deny]: `engine` depends on `backends`
  --> src/engine/mixer.rs:42:17
   |
42 |         let io = backends::Alsa::open();
   |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ `backends::Alsa`
   = rule: deps.rule[0] "core must not use adapter" (brickie.toml:21)
   = help: depend on the port trait and receive the implementation from the assembly
   = note: modules: engine::mixer -> backends::alsa (uses, prod)
```

- Header: level (`error` fails CI, `warning` does not), the code in brackets, a message.
- `-->` is the primary location `file:line:col`; extra locations follow ("and N more").
- `rule` names the configured rule that fired and where it is; it holds the maintainers' reason.
- `help` is the suggested fix; `note` adds context (for example the full cycle path).
- Every finding has a stable 8-hex `id` (in JSON, and in `brickie.review.toml` once accepted).
- The last line summarises: `error: 1 error, 3 warnings; 0 accepted`.

Vocabulary:

- A brick is a named group of crates or modules from `[[brick]]`. An edge is a reference from a
  module in one brick to an item in a module of another.
- Edge kinds (one per reference site): `uses` (call, type, constant), `implements`
  (`impl Trait for X` where the trait lives elsewhere), `reexports` (a `use` with any `pub`
  visibility; private `use` leaves count as `uses`).
- The edge target is always the module that DEFINES the item, even when reached through a
  re-export; a finding's note shows `written <path as written> -> defined in <module>`.
- Scope is `prod`, or `test` for `#[cfg(test)]`, `tests/` and `benches/`; test edges are checked
  like prod edges. Edges inside one brick, or touching a module in no brick, are ignored.
- Nested bricks: a brick with `path = "<dir>"` is a composite; its children, rules and `exports`
  are in `<dir>/brickie.toml`. A finding's JSON `brick_level` (`root`, `root/web`) is the tree
  level it is reported at; its brick names are children of that level and `rule` points at the
  config file owning the rule. An edge is checked against the rules of the lowest common ancestor
  of its two bricks (`web/ui` to `core` is checked as `web -> core` in the root file).

## Diagnostic codes and how to fix them

### deps/deny (error by default)

An edge matches a `[[deps.rule]]` with `action = "deny"`. Remove the dependency: depend on a
trait, type or function in a brick you may use, and have the assembling brick pass the concrete
implementation in. If the code is test-only, use `#[cfg(test)]` or move it under `tests/` (many
rules apply only to `prod`). If the dependency is truly intended, report it for a human reviewer;
do not edit the rule.

### deps/default

An edge matches no rule and `deps.default = "deny"`. Same fix as `deps/deny`: either it is a
layering mistake (remove it) or the maintainers need an `allow` rule (report it; do not add it).

### deps/private

The edge reaches into a composite brick through a child not listed in its `exports` (the message
names the composite and the hidden child; `rule` is the composite's config file). Use what the
composite exports. Re-exporting the item through an exported child does not help: the edge points
at the defining module. If the child should be visible, report it; the maintainers may add it to
`exports`, or a scoped entry `{ brick = "x", scope = "test" }` for test code only.

### deps/cycle

Two or more bricks depend on each other, directly or through others; the note shows the cycle.
Break it: move the shared type into a trait or type owned by the lower brick, or invert one
dependency so the lower brick receives what it needs from the higher one (parameter, trait object,
callback). Do not merge bricks in `brickie.toml`. Cycles are found per level, among the children
of one composite (`brick_level` says which).

### complexity/cognitive, complexity/cyclomatic, complexity/nesting, complexity/paths, complexity/params, complexity/lines

One finding per function and metric above the limit of a `[[complexity]]` rule (inclusive:
"limit 15" fails at 16). The message gives the value and the limit. Metrics:

- `cognitive`: how hard the function is to read. `+1 + nesting` per `if`, `match` (once, not per
  arm), `for`, `while`, `loop`, `let ... else`; `+1` per `else`; `+1` per sequence of like `&&` /
  `||`; `+1` per labeled `break`/`continue` and per direct recursive call. `?` is free. Closures
  add nesting but no cost themselves (as in SonarSource). Macro bodies (token trees such as
  `println!(..)`, `vec![..]`, `view! {..}`) are not parsed, so branching inside them is not
  measured. Fix:
  guard clauses and early `return`/`continue`, `?` instead of nested matches, extract a cohesive step.
- `cyclomatic`: `1 + if + loops + (match arms - 1) + let-else + && + || + ?`. Fix: replace long
  chains with a lookup table, data-driven code, or split by responsibility.
- `nesting`: deepest nesting of branches, loops and closures. Fix: invert conditions and return
  early, flatten with `let ... else`, extract the inner body when it is a meaningful unit.
- `paths` (simplified NPath): an estimate of execution paths. An `if` is `then + else` (an absent
  `else` counts 1); a `match` is the sum of its arms, and a `match` of 3 or more constant arms
  counts 1; a loop is `body + 1`; each `?`, `&&` and `||` adds 1. Sequential decisions add; they
  do not multiply as in textbook NPath. Fix: reduce independent branches in one function, separate unrelated decisions into
  functions with a clear contract, use tables for constant `match` arms.
- `params`: parameters other than `self`. Fix: group related parameters into a struct or options
  type that has a meaning in the domain (not a bag of unrelated values).
- `lines`: lines of the function. Fix: split along real responsibilities.

The rules of every level above a function apply to it (each level selects its own child on the
path); per metric the tightest limit wins, so a nested config can only tighten. Test-scope
functions are checked only when the rule's `scope` includes tests. Never raise a limit; never add
`#[cfg(test)]` or move code only to change its scope.

### stale/file (warning)

A `.rs` file was changed, added or deleted after `brickie measure` (the message says which), so
its data is old. Run `brickie measure`, then `brickie check`.

### bricks/unmapped (warning)

A module belongs to no brick, so none of its edges or functions are checked (usually after adding
a file or module). Add it to the `members` of its `[[brick]]` only when the right brick is obvious
from the surrounding code; otherwise ask the reviewer. No re-measure is needed.

### interface/unused (warning)

A leaf brick declares an item (reachable from outside: public API of its crate, or a `pub` /
`pub(crate)` item whose module is visible to another brick) that no code outside the brick and no
test uses (tests anywhere count, including the brick's own). The location is the definition. Fix:
if only the brick needs it, narrow its visibility (private, `pub(super)`, or a private module); if
dead, delete it; if real public API, add a test that exercises it. Methods, fields and variants
count as uses of their type; `pub use` re-exports are not uses.

### config/missing, config/overlap, config/unassigned, config/member-outside-parent, config/unknown-export

Configuration errors (exit 2, printed on stderr with the code first; no findings are reported):

- `config/missing`: a brick has `path = "<dir>"` but `<dir>/brickie.toml` does not exist.
- `config/overlap`: a module matches two bricks of one file with equal specificity.
- `config/unassigned`: a module of a composite is in none of its children (children must
  partition the composite).
- `config/member-outside-parent`: a child's member matches a module outside its composite.
- `config/unknown-export`: `exports` names something that is not a brick of that file.

These are brick-structure decisions: report them rather than editing the config to silence them.

In an open change the preview is a draft: `config/unassigned`, `config/overlap` and
`config/member-outside-parent` do not stop it. They appear as `[config]` items of
`brickie change --todo` and `pending:` lines of `brickie check --change`, and publish refuses
(`change/invalid: config/...`) until fixed: give each unassigned module to one of the composite's
bricks (`set_brick` members), make overlapping members distinct, keep child members inside their
composite.

### change/planned, change/planned-edge, change/no-reason, change/conflict, change/proposed, change/outside-edit, change/invalid, change/open, change/none

Change sessions (see "Change sessions"):

- `change/planned` (a `check --change` note and a `--todo` task): a brick of the design has no
  measured module. Create its code as its members say (or let publish scaffold it), then
  `brickie measure`.
- `change/planned-edge` (`--todo` `link` task): an allow rule the change adds has no measured code
  edge yet. Write the code using the target if intended, then `brickie measure`; otherwise leave
  it (allowing is not requiring).
- `change/no-reason` (`--todo` `reason` task and a publish warning, not a blocker): a rule the
  change adds has no `reason`. Propose a `set_rule` with a one-line reason at that `index`.
- `change/conflict`: an op no longer replays because the element it edits changed (usually an
  earlier op was rejected). Publish refuses. Stop and ask the human.
- `change/proposed`: publish refuses while an op awaits review; the human reviews it.
- `change/outside-edit`: a config file was edited by hand while the change was open; publish
  refuses. Report it; the human restores the file or discards the change.
- `change/invalid`: the published design would not load (for example a rule naming an unknown
  brick). Propose a fixing op or ask the human.
- `change/open`: `brickie change open` while a change is open. `change/none`: a `brickie change`
  command with no change open; then work as in "Workflow".

## brickie.toml reference

```toml
include = ["presets/layered.toml"]  # optional; paths relative to this file; merged first
exports = ["api", { brick = "internal", scope = "test" }]
                               # composite files only: children visible from outside (default
                               # none); a scoped entry counts for edges of that scope only

[[brick]]
name = "engine"                # unique in this file
members = ["my-engine", "my-app::api", "module:my-app::entry", "path:crates/engine/"]
                               # package name (all targets) | module prefix (and descendants) |
                               # exact module id | path:<dir>/ (crates whose manifest is under the
                               # folder, relative to this file). Most specific wins (path: <
                               # package < module prefix < exact module; longer wins); a tie
                               # across bricks is an error
tags = ["core"]                # optional labels for rule selectors
desc = "Rule evaluation"       # optional one-liner shown in the viewer; no effect on checks

[[brick]]
name = "web"
path = "crates/web"            # composite: children in crates/web/brickie.toml (required);
                               # members default to ["path:crates/web/"]

[deps]
default = "allow"              # allow | deny: for edges that match no rule
cycles = "deny"                # allow | deny: cycles between bricks (prod edges)

[[deps.rule]]
from = "tag:app"               # selector: brick name | tag:<tag> | *
to = "tag:core"
kinds = ["uses", "implements"] # uses | implements | reexports; default all
scope = "prod"                 # prod (default) | test | all
action = "allow"               # allow | deny
reason = "app calls into core" # shown in findings
help = "optional fix hint"     # replaces the built-in hint

[[complexity]]
bricks = "tag:core"            # selector; default *
cognitive = 15                 # any of cognitive, cyclomatic, nesting, paths, params, lines
nesting = 3
scope = "prod"                 # prod (default) | test | all
level = "error"                # error (fails check) | warn; default error
help = "optional fix hint"
```

Names, tags and rules are local to a file: its rules select only its own bricks. Every
`brickie.toml` (root or composite) has the same schema; `include` works in each.

Matching: for edges, the rule with the highest specificity wins (brick name 3, tag 2, `*` 1 per
side, summed); deny wins a tie. For complexity, per function and metric the most specific rule
that sets the metric applies (the lower limit on a tie). Unknown fields, tags, bricks or kinds are
configuration errors (exit 2).

`brickie.review.toml` (next to `brickie.toml`) lists findings a human accepted:

```toml
[[accept]]
id = "3fa9c1d2"                # finding id
reason = "why this is fine"
```

Accepted findings do not fail `check`. Do not create or edit this file yourself.
